outcome: Indications for obstetric hysterectomy (Placenta Accreta Spectrum, Postpartum Hemorrhage, Uterine Rupture)
Perioperative variables (intraoperative blood loss, total blood & blood product requirements, ICU admission, inotropic requirements)
cohort: The study included 37 women undergoing obstetric hysterectomy following caesarean or vaginal deliveries, mid-trimester, or within 42 days of delivery or termination of pregnancy.
finding: Emergency obstetric hysterectomy was associated with significantly higher maternal morbidity, including greater intraoperative blood loss, increased need for blood products, more ICU admissions, higher inotropic requirements, and more postoperative complications, as well as higher maternal mortality, compared to elective obstetric hysterectomy.
